target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures focus on the benefits of edge computing/device processing, specifically noting proximity to data, reduced response time, and improved privacy, security, and personalization.

Both disclosures describe mobile devices (handsets/PCs in 2024, mobile in 2023) becoming pervasive AI platforms where complex large generative AI algorithms run on-device to enable on-demand and contextual use cases.

Both disclosures outline the vision of generative AI becoming ubiquitous and expanding beyond smartphones into other industries such as IoT, XR, and automotive.

Both disclosures address the broader trend of generative AI capabilities in edge devices, with 2023 discussing the general vision of AI expansion and 2024 providing specific adoption forecasts for generative AI capable smartphones.

previous_disclosures.summary: Qualcomm envisions mobile becoming a pervasive AI platform where complex large generative AI algorithms run on-device, with 5G connectivity complementing on-device AI for productivity and contextual use cases. The company expects generative AI to become ubiquitous, expanding beyond smartphones into industries such as compute, IoT, XR, and automotive.

current_disclosures.summary: Edge device computing allows for context-aware processing, reducing response time and improving privacy, security, and personalization compared to cloud-based applications.
Mobile handsets and PCs are becoming pervasive AI platforms with complex large generative AI algorithms running on-device to enable on-demand use cases at lower energy costs.
Qualcomm envisions generative AI becoming ubiquitous, expanding beyond smartphones and PCs into industries such as IoT, XR, and automotive.
Qualcomm expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities, with analysts estimating 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2024 disclosures cover the landscape of AI model investment (LLMs, SLMs, etc.), their disruption of user experiences, and the strategic view that these models must run on-device for privacy and utility. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) covers the exact same specific points: the development of LLMs/SLMs/LVMs/LMMs, their disruption of search/content, and the necessity of on-device execution for utility, privacy, and security. qcom_2024_1_D011 maps to the model landscape/disruption, and qcom_2024_1_D012 maps to the on-device necessity/utility argument found in qcom_2025_1_D010.

The 2024 disclosure expects continued advancement in edge device generative AI capabilities and increased adoption. The 2025 disclosure (qcom_2025_1_D010) contains the specific sentence: 'We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.' This is a direct textual and topical match.

While developed primarily for the cloud, these models must run on-device to maximize utility, privacy, and security, and the company expects continued advancement and adoption of generative AI capabilities in edge devices.

comparisons.peer_summary: AMD continued investing in the open ROCm software stack, making key optimizations and adding features in the latest release to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and AMD are heavily investing in generative AI capabilities for edge devices, though Qualcomm focuses on the market adoption forecast and AMD on the enabling software stack. Qualcomm highlights that analysts estimate 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024, reflecting its view on the rapid expansion of edge AI adoption. Similarly, AMD reports continued investment in the ROCm open software stack to improve performance for generative AI workloads and simplify the developer experience for AMD platforms. While Qualcomm cites specific market penetration metrics for handsets, AMD details its technical efforts in software optimizations and framework support to drive these workloads.

sentences.text: We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.
For example, analysts estimate that 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024 (Counterpoint, October 2024).

We continued to invest in driving software capabilities and the open ecosystem to deliver powerful new features and capabilities in the AMD ROCm™ open software stack, bringing the latest features to highly-performant AI training and inference on AMD platforms.

During the year, we made several key optimizations and additional features in the latest AMD ROCm software that increases performance in key generative AI workloads, adds expanded support and optimization for additional frameworks and libraries, and simplifies the overall developer experience.

comparisons.peer_summary: The Tanzu Platform accelerates software delivery with enhanced governance and operational efficiency, includes Tanzu AI Solutions for generative AI applications, and offers full-stack visibility and lifecycle management across clouds.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Broadcom are integrating generative AI into their product ecosystems, though Qualcomm focuses on edge device capabilities while Broadcom focuses on application delivery platforms. Qualcomm expects continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices, emphasizing the hardware-level adoption in handsets. Broadcom highlights its Tanzu AI Solutions, which help application teams deliver generative AI-powered applications quickly and at scale. While both disclosures reflect the industry-wide trend of incorporating generative AI, Qualcomm's focus is on the proliferation of AI in consumer edge devices, whereas Broadcom's focus is on the software platform enabling enterprise application development for AI.

sentences.text: We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.

• Tanzu Platform: This cloud native application platform accelerates software delivery, providing platform engineering teams with enhanced governance and operational efficiency while reducing toil and complexity for development teams. Tanzu Platform includes access to content including enterprise-ready curated distributions of open source software technologies used for storing and processing data. It also includes Tanzu AI Solutions, a set of capabilities that help application teams deliver generative AI-powered, intelligent applications quickly, safely, and at scale. Tanzu Platform also offers teams full-stack visibility from applications to infrastructure and efficient modern application lifecycle management across public and private clouds with Cloud Foundry and/or with any conformant Kubernetes.

comparisons.peer_summary: Intel views AI as a generational shift and aims to bring AI to where data is generated and used, addressing the full AI continuum from GenAI to AI PCs and edge computing. The company leverages a spectrum of hardware and software platforms for open, modular solutions and is infusing AI into its technologies to support current and future workloads.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Intel view AI as a generational shift extending to edge devices, including AI PCs, and are infusing AI into their respective technologies to support these emerging usages. Intel states that it seeks to address every phase of the AI continuum, including emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge, believing AI represents a generational shift in computing. Similarly, Qualcomm expects continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption in handsets. While Intel frames this as a broad strategic shift across the continuum and Qualcomm focuses on the specific growth in handset AI capabilities, both companies identify the expansion of AI into consumer edge computing as a critical business driver.

sentences.text: We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.
We also seek to address every phase of the AI continuum, from the largest, most challenging GenAI and large language models to emerging usages like AI PCs and AI at the edge.
We believe AI represents a generational shift in computing by expanding human abilities and solving the most challenging problems.

We are infusing AI into Intel technologies, supporting today's GenAI workloads, fueling emerging usages like AI PC and AI at the edge, and pioneering innovations that we believe will help advance the future of AI in the next decade.

comparisons.peer_topic: Demand drivers for mobile memory and storage
comparisons.peer_summary: Proliferation of smartphones and tablets increases demand for high-performance memory, with on-device AI capabilities driving needs for increased memory and storage capacity.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and Micron identify on-device AI capabilities in mobile devices as a primary driver for increased demand for higher performance memory and storage. Qualcomm explicitly states that it expects continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption in handsets. Micron corroborates this trend, noting that smartphones offering personalized AI capabilities executed on the device are driving increased memory and storage capacity needs. Both disclosures link the proliferation of mobile AI directly to hardware demand, with Qualcomm focusing on the adoption forecast and Micron on the resulting infrastructure requirements for memory.

sentences.text: We expect continued advancement in the generative AI capabilities of edge devices and increased adoption of generative AI capable technologies in handsets and other edge devices.
For example, analysts estimate that 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable, up from 19% in 2024 (Counterpoint, October 2024).
Smartphones offer tremendous potential for personalized AI capabilities that offer greater security and responsiveness when executed on the device.
Enabling these on-device AI capabilities is driving increased memory and storage capacity needs and increasing demand for new value-add solutions.

comparisons.peer_topic: RTX AI ecosystem and market position
comparisons.peer_summary: RTX GPUs accelerate AI applications, and with an installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs and 500+ RTX AI-enabled applications, RTX is the AI PC leader.
comparisons.comparison: Both Qualcomm and NVIDIA position themselves as leaders in the AI PC market, with NVIDIA claiming leadership based on its installed base and application ecosystem, while Qualcomm forecasts the widespread adoption of generative AI in handsets. NVIDIA states that with an installed base of over 100 million AI-capable PCs and more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications, it is the AI PC leader. Qualcomm complements this view by highlighting the anticipated trajectory of the market, noting that analysts estimate 46% of smartphones sold in 2027 will be generative AI capable. Both disclosures underscore the significant scale and momentum of AI integration in consumer edge devices, with NVIDIA emphasizing its current dominant position and Qualcomm emphasizing the future growth rate.

RTX GPUs will also accelerate a new generation of AI applications.
With an installed base of over 100 million AI capable PCs, more than 500 RTX AI-enabled applications and games, and a robust suite of development tools, RTX is already the AI PC leader.
